statement: In New York City, daily emergency department visits for heat-related illness (DOHMH syndromic surveillance) rise steeply with the day's maximum temperature in the warm season.

graph_evidence.summary: Sun et al. 2021 (BMJ, 74 million insured US adults, 2010-2019): days at the local 95th percentile of warm-season temperature had 66.3% (60.2 to 72.7) excess risk of ED visits for heat-related illness, with stronger effects in the Northeast. Stowell et al. 2023 (US children): OR 1.34 (1.16 to 1.56), ages 6-12.
Kingsley et al. 2016 (Rhode Island 2005-2012): Tmax 75 to 85 F associated with 23.9% higher rates of heat-related ED visits (Poisson). The graph stores 23.9 as a coefficient without units.
Extreme heat raises mortality across 14 studies (RR 1.1 to 1.4 typical). Context; heat mortality in NYC is published only as yearly citywide counts.

literature.citation: Sun S et al. Ambient heat and risks of emergency department visits among adults in the United States. BMJ 2021;375:e065653.
literature.finding: 95th vs median warm-season temperature (34.4 C vs 14.9 C national average): heat-related illness ED visits +66.3% (60.2 to 72.7).

literature.citation: Kingsley SL et al. Current and projected heat-related morbidity and mortality in Rhode Island. Environ Health Perspect 2016;124:460-467.
literature.finding: Tmax 75 to 85 F (5.6 C): heat-related ED visits +23.9%.

prediction.magnitude: Warm season (May-September), IRR per 5 C Central Park TMAX between 1.5 and 5. The curve is flat below about 27 C and steep above it; on days at the city's 95th percentile TMAX versus the warm-season median, RR at least 1.66 (Sun et al. national average) and probably above 3, because syndromic counts are near zero on mild days.
prediction.support_if: lower 95% limit of the IRR per 5 C above 1.00 and estimate >= 1.5 (hit); estimate between 1.0 and 1.5 with lower limit above 1 is partial

plan: Data: EHDP-data GitHub repository (nychealth/EHDP-data, branch production, key-topics/heat-syndrome: previous_years.csv, edheat1720_supp.csv, edheatYYYY_live.csv), daily counts of heat-syndrome ED visits citywide, cited by commit SHA. If no daily series exists, use EHDP indicator 2075 (yearly heat ED visits) and say so. Weather: NOAA GHCN-Daily Central Park TMAX (the DOHMH file's own LaGuardia heat-index column is used only as a cross-check, not as the exposure). Model: negative binomial GLM of daily counts, May-September, on linear TMAX/5 with day-of-week, month and year factors; and a natural spline (4 df) for the curve, RR vs the warm-season median TMAX; RR at the 95th percentile compared with Sun et al. Secondary: EHDP yearly heat ED visits (indicator 2075, citywide) and yearly heat deaths (2074) against the number of days with TMAX >= 32.2 C (90 F) per year, Spearman correlation, descriptive.
alternatives: Syndromic case definition changed in 2023 (applied back to all years, per DOHMH)
Chief-complaint keyword matching may respond to heat warnings and media attention, not only to illness (awareness bias)
Some residents seek care outside the city; coverage of 100% of NYC EDs only from May 2016
